newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs drop on BOJ rate comment.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs drop on BOJ rate comment.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures fell sharply in Wednesday afternoon trade following remarks on interest rates by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui, dealers said.
Fukui was quoted as saying the central bank was considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but it did not want to make a hasty decision.

He made the comment at a meeting with executives of Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, the Japanese Trade Union Confederation (Rengo), at which the labour group urged the BOJ to raise the discount rate.
"The BOJ deputy governor's comment caused Euroyen to drop to a low," a trader with a U.S. house said.

December Euroyen stood at 98.98 at 0610 GMT after falling as low as 98.86 against a high of 98.99 earlier in the day and an IMM close at 98.97. Volume was a moderate 16,025 lots with participation somewhat muted by a holiday in Singapore.
June JGBs were quoted at 123.42 against an early high of 124.91 and a previous close at 124.45.
Euroyen and JGB futures were boosted early in the day by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term interest rates unchanged at its policy-making meeting on Tuesday.
Dealers said this removed any pressure on the BOJ to raise rates for the time being, particularly in light of the yen's recent heavy gains against the dollar.
